name: Amir Zare

paragraphs: AI and Data Engineer with 7+ years of experience building backend systems, data pipelines and analytics products. Founder of DataLayer, an analytics platform for e-commerce sellers. Hands-on with Python, advanced SQL, BigQuery, dbt, Airflow and A/B test analysis, plus production LLM applications. Armenian permanent resident, based in Yerevan and ready to work.

Experienced in designing ETL/ELT pipelines, orchestrating workflows with Apache Airflow, building APIs and backend architectures, and developing analytics-focused systems using Python, SQL, and cloud technologies.

Transitioned from enterprise backend engineering into modern data platform development, focusing on scalable analytics systems, orchestration frameworks, cloud infrastructure, and AI-assisted data applications. Interested in Data Platform Engineering, AI Engineering, and scalable distributed systems.

projects.name: AgentPages
projects.subtitle: Static Site Publishing API for AI Agents
bullets: Built an HTTP API that lets AI agents publish static websites: an agent sends the site files as JSON, gets back a live URL, and can update or delete the site later.
Separated the API service from the sites service. The sites service is read-only, only reads published files and never touches the database.
Served untrusted uploaded pages from a separate origin inside a CSP sandbox, and built a sandbox test page that checks the isolation guarantees (opaque origin; storage, cookies and fetch blocked).
Added API-key bearer authentication, upload size limits, and a web dashboard for publishing, updating and deleting sites from a folder.

projects.name: Chess vs AI
projects.subtitle: LLM Game Opponent
bullets: Built a playable pygame chess game with three opponents: a random mover, Stockfish, and an LLM through OpenRouter that comments on its moves.

Made the LLM opponent reliable: the model gets the board position (FEN), the move history and the legal moves, and answers in structured JSON. The code checks each move is legal, retries up to 3 times, then falls back to a random move, and the UI shows how many illegal attempts there were.
Records the full game in standard chess notation (PGN) and keeps API keys local in an env file.

projects.name: Voice Narrator
projects.subtitle: Local Voice Cloning for Tutorial Production
bullets: Built a fully local voice-cloning narration tool for programming tutorials, so there are no recurring fees and recordings never leave the machine.

Designed a two-stage pipeline after testing showed direct cloning gave inconsistent accents: the base TTS model speaks each sentence, then voice conversion re-voices it to match the reference recording.
Added batch processing (the model loads once, and one failing script doesn’t stop the rest), config-driven defaults, a custom pronunciation dictionary, and MP3 export.
Checked the model licenses and kept the built-in AI-audio watermark on every output.

projects.name: UIGen
projects.subtitle: AI React Component Generator
projects.note: Anthropic “Claude Code in Action” course project
bullets: Worked on an AI-powered React component generator that uses Claude, with a live preview, a virtual file system, a code editor and saved projects.
Maintained dependency security by pinning versions and patching a critical Next.js vulnerability (CVE-2025-55182) instead of running blanket audit fixes.

projects.name: A/B Test Analysis
projects.subtitle: Cookie Cats Game Gate Experiment
bullets: Analyzed a public mobile-game A/B test with 90,189 players to see whether moving the first progress gate from level 30 to 40 affects retention and engagement.
Found a statistically significant 0.82 pp (4.3% relative) drop in 7-day retention (95% CI −1.33 to −0.31 pp; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0047), and recommended keeping the gate at level 30.

Ran experiment-validity checks: sample ratio mismatch (chi-square), duplicate and missing data checks, outlier handling with medians and rank tests, minimum-detectable-effect power analysis, and Holm-Bonferroni correction for multiple tests.
Labelled post-treatment segmentation as descriptive only, and published an interactive Tableau Public dashboard.

projects.name: MoodScape
projects.subtitle: Music Mood Clustering Toolkit
bullets: Built a configurable clustering toolkit that groups music tracks by mood from numeric audio features, with YAML/CLI batch runs that keep each run’s outputs separate.
Added preprocessing options (standard or min-max scaling, feature selection, PCA), silhouette-based K selection, and evaluation with silhouette, Davies–Bouldin and Calinski–Harabasz scores.
Built run comparison (Adjusted Rand Index, NMI, pairwise stability heatmaps), named snapshots of saved models for predicting on new data, and exportable evidence reports.
Wrote unit tests for preprocessing, snapshots and comparison utilities.

projects.name: Multi-Label Text Classification System
projects.subtitle: Content Moderation
bullets: Built an end-to-end multi-label classifier for moderation labels on online comments: load → clean → vectorize → train → evaluate → save.
Used TF-IDF features with a One-vs-Rest logistic regression baseline, with per-label evaluation and error analysis.
Saved the model and vectorizer as artifacts for reproducible inference.

projects.name: ML Music Recommender

projects.name: Hands-On Machine Learning

projects.name: Barbershop Queue
projects.subtitle: Booking & Queue Management System
bullets: Built a full-stack booking and walk-in queue system: customers book or check in online, and admins get an email for each new check-in.
Developed a FastAPI backend with SQLAlchemy (SQLite in development, ready for Postgres) for check-in, queue position, call-next, done and no-show flows.
Built a React admin panel (dashboard, history, customers, settings) protected by signed session-cookie authentication, plus a no-JavaScript check-in page as a fallback.
Built an animated public marketing site with React, Tailwind and Framer Motion, with a booking form connected to the same API. The backend serves both the API and the built frontend.
Added switchable email providers (Resend or SendGrid) with a dry-run mode for development.

projects.name: Mayad Tour
projects.subtitle: Travel Agency Website

projects.name: Mail.tm Temporary Email Service

Added typed exceptions for invalid state and HTTP failures.

projects.name: Laravel Design Patterns Series
bullets: Implemented Gang of Four design patterns in Laravel. For example, Observer handles user-model lifecycle events, and Factory switches between payment gateways (PayPal/Stripe) at runtime.

projects.name: FlowFleet
projects.subtitle: Real-Time Logistics Data Platform
bullets: Designed and built a production-style real-time streaming platform for a fictional delivery company, delivered in 8 phases, each with working code, tests and architecture notes.
Implemented change data capture from PostgreSQL/PostGIS with Debezium, covering snapshot vs. streaming modes, tombstones, and replication slot and connector recovery.
Designed Kafka topics with Avro and Schema Registry, built a high-volume driver-location simulator, and tested consumer-group rebalancing.
Developed Apache Flink jobs in Java 21 using keyed state, event-time windows, watermarks, timers and side outputs, including broadcast-state geofencing with JTS.
Built sinks to TimescaleDB and ClickHouse with batching, retries and idempotent writes, plus BigQuery for analytics.
Engineered for failure: a dead-letter queue for poison messages, late-data handling, checkpoint and savepoint recovery, and backpressure experiments.
Deployed on Kubernetes with Helm, the Flink Kubernetes Operator (savepoint-based upgrades) and Argo CD (app-of-apps GitOps).

Load-tested from 1k to 50k events/second with a live-adjustable rate generator, end-to-end p50/p95/p99 latency histograms and a ramp harness. Tuned throughput and added the Flink autoscaler and consumer HPA.
Added Prometheus and Grafana observability across the pipeline.

projects.name: AI Phone Assistant
projects.subtitle: Voice Agent Booking System
bullets: Built an AI phone assistant for a barbershop on Suisse Line’s voice agent platform for Suisse IT’s Challenge A. Callers can check services and availability, book, find and cancel appointments, and join a waitlist.
Designed a FastAPI booking backend that exposes seven live tools to the agent during calls, with one database as the single source of truth for the website, staff dashboard and phone channel.
Prevented double bookings with an atomic booking lock, verified with 12 simultaneous booking requests and with website and phone bookings at the same moment.
Made booking and cancellation idempotent so the agent can safely retry after timeouts without creating duplicate appointments.
Designed a structured ok/error-code response contract so the agent can always tell the caller what happened, and added a read-back confirmation step before any booking.
Shipped a Smart Cancellation Waitlist: consent-first sign-up, freed slots offered oldest-first with time-limited offers, first confirmed booking wins, and 30-day data retention.
Secured the public endpoint with token-scoped routes and request-size limits, exposed only the assistant service through a Cloudflare tunnel, and kept names and phone numbers out of logs.

projects.name: EvidenceHub
projects.subtitle: MySQL Performance & Sharding Platform
bullets: Building a reference data platform that migrates a deliberately poor legacy MySQL schema to an optimized, sharded design. Every performance claim is backed by a measured benchmark report.
Set up a 4-shard MySQL 8 cluster with a catalog database and Redis in Docker Compose, plus a synthetic data generator that scales to 20M rows.

Defined 8 mission-critical queries, each with a latency SLO (p95 under 50 ms for point and latest-N lookups), and built a Locust + EXPLAIN ANALYZE benchmark harness that produced the baseline performance report.
Enforced strict engineering standards: mypy --strict, Ruff, Pytest/Hypothesis, GitHub Actions CI with full-history secret scanning, and architecture decision records.
Roadmap: online schema migration, shard routing and resharding, Kafka ingestion with a DLQ, a Redis-cached FastAPI layer, and a Spark/Iceberg Kimball warehouse orchestrated by Airflow.

projects.name: DataLayer Evolution Agent
projects.subtitle: Internal Growth Intelligence System
bullets: Designed and shipped a production system that automates DataLayer's own growth decision-making: a daily batch job pulling product, marketing, and lead data, synthesized via LLM into one prioritized "Growth Brief" emailed to the team each morning

Deliberately minimal, production-safe stack (Flask, PostgreSQL, APScheduler, Docker) — explicitly excluded heavier frameworks (LangChain, vector DBs, Redis, Celery, Kubernetes, multi-agent orchestration) to keep the system auditable, low-risk, and easy to reason about
Implemented least-privilege data access via separately-scoped read-only and write database roles, so a bug in the write path can never compromise the read-only analysis guarantee
Engineered graceful degradation across multiple data sources (internal database, GA4, Search Console, Reddit) — a failed source is logged and surfaced rather than crashing the pipeline

Solved LLM reliability limitations by moving mechanical judgment out of the prompt and into code: metrics precomputed and passed as exact figures, outputs re-sorted deterministically, and a dedicated anti-overclaiming design preventing the model from claiming false causation on low-traffic data
Found and fixed a real data-integrity bug where internal test accounts were being miscounted as paying customers
Delivered in three phases over one month, followed by a structured 8-angle code review that surfaced and fixed 10 bugs pre-production
Live in production, running daily against real company data
Extended the agent to find leads and draft customized outreach emails for each prospect; every message is reviewed before it is sent.

projects.name: Crypto Analytics Data Platform

Built scalable data ingestion pipelines for cryptocurrency market data using Apache Kafka and batch ingestion workflows.
Developed distributed data processing pipelines with Apache Spark for large-scale transformation and analytics workloads.
Orchestrated ETL/ELT workflows using Apache Airflow, enabling automated scheduling, monitoring, and dependency management.
Implemented a Lakehouse architecture utilizing Parquet and DuckDB for efficient storage, analytical querying, and data versioning.
Built data transformation layers using dbt, applying modular modeling, testing, and documentation best practices.
Provisioned and managed cloud infrastructure on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) using Terraform following Infrastructure-as-Code principles.
Designed dimensional data models and analytics-ready datasets to support reporting and business intelligence use cases.
Developed interactive dashboards and reporting interfaces for cryptocurrency market insights and trend analysis.
Currently extending the platform with Snowflake integration, AI-assisted anomaly detection, retrieval-augmented analytics (RAG), and embedding-based search capabilities.
Applied modular architecture principles to support scalability, maintainability, and future cloud-native deployment.
Built a crypto market-data pipeline with hourly Spark ingestion running on GitHub Actions.
Modeled the data in dbt as a 4-layer medallion pipeline (staging, bronze, silver, gold), with not_null and unique tests running in CI against DuckDB and BigQuery.
Published dbt documentation on GitHub Pages.
Stored data as Parquet and queried it with DuckDB.
Built dashboards for cryptocurrency market trends.

Built ingestion pipelines to process raw CSV activity datasets and convert them into optimized Parquet files within a local data lake architecture.
Developed SQL-based transformation workflows that materialized analytical summary tables inside DuckDB data warehouses.
Created aggregated analytical models including daily_user_summary, daily_activity_counts, and daily_wrist_counts.
Implemented Apache Airflow DAGs orchestrating dataset download, ingestion, and transformation stages.
Developed interactive analytics dashboards using Streamlit for monitoring activity trends and user behavior.
Built lightweight REST-style JSON endpoints using Flask for programmatic data access.
Utilized Parquet-based lakehouse patterns to reduce storage footprint and improve analytical query performance.

Applied modern Data Engineering concepts including ETL / ELT, Data Lakes, Data Warehousing, Workflow Orchestration, Batch Processing, Analytics Engineering, and Data Modeling.

Applied modern Data Engineering and Analytics Engineering practices including ETL Pipelines, Data Warehousing, Analytics APIs, Feature Engineering, Forecasting Models, Dashboard Development, and Data Visualization.

projects.name: Job Hunter
projects.subtitle: 7-Agent AI Job Search Platform

Demonstrates end-to-end agentic AI system design: agent orchestration, tool-calling, inter-agent communication, and async task execution.

Worked with an agent server and debug console that showed every tool call, SSE chat and A2A endpoints, and a seeded SQLite dataset, and checked my work against deterministic tests.

Built advanced filtering, search, pagination, and categorization APIs.
Implemented comprehensive testing using PHPUnit and Mockery.
Developed scalable REST APIs supporting frontend news applications.
Added centralized logging, error handling, and monitoring capabilities.

projects.name: Laravel Queue Performance Benchmark System
bullets: Built a Laravel-based benchmarking system to compare synchronous and asynchronous processing strategies for large-scale datasets.
Seeded and processed high-volume datasets including 200,000 Orders, 1,000,000 Items, and 1,000 Products.
Implemented invoice generation workflows for thousands of orders and evaluated application performance under heavy workloads.
Compared Laravel Eloquent ORM and Query Builder approaches for large dataset processing.
Designed queue-based background processing pipelines using Redis and Laravel Queue Workers.
Integrated Laravel Horizon for queue monitoring, job management, and operational visibility.
Implemented asynchronous PDF generation workflows using Laravel DomPDF.
Demonstrated significant reduction in request execution time and elimination of timeout issues through background job processing.

Applied backend engineering concepts including Asynchronous Processing, Distributed Task Execution, Queue-Based Architectures, Redis, Performance Optimization, Background Job Processing, and Scalability Engineering.

projects.name: Env Loader PHP Package
bullets: Developed a lightweight PHP package for parsing and managing .env configuration files in Laravel and PHP applications.
Implemented a custom environment loader supporting Multi-line environment variables, Quoted values handling, Comment and whitespace parsing, and Robust error handling for malformed inputs.
Designed a service-based architecture to ensure modularity, extensibility, and clean separation of concerns.
Built a configuration system allowing structured access to environment values using dot-notation (e.g. file.name.default).
Implemented factory pattern for flexible instantiation of environment loaders.
Added custom exception handling for Missing configuration files, Regex parsing errors, and Invalid environment formats.
Designed the package to be reusable across Laravel and plain PHP applications.
Applied clean architecture principles and PSR-style modular design.
Developed unit tests using PHPUnit to ensure reliability of parsing logic and edge cases.
